Cada 30 de agosto se conmemora en Argentina el Día del Ferrocarril, en honor al primer viaje de una locomotora en el país

Este acontecimiento marcó el inicio de una nueva era en el transporte argentino, que más tarde conectaría diversas regiones de la Nación

El 29 de agosto de 1857, la locomotora "La Porteña" realizó el trayecto inaugural, un viaje de 35 minutos que alcanzó una velocidad máxima de 20 km/h. Partió de la Estación del Parque, hoy Plaza Lavalle cerca del Teatro Colón, y el destino fue la estación San José de Flores en el barrio de Floresta

La elección de esta fecha se refiere al evento formal que tuvo lugar el día después del primer recorrido en tren del país

La locomotora, propiedad de la Sociedad Camino de Hierro del Ferrocarril Oeste, fue construida en Gran Bretaña y llegó a Argentina en 1856. York / Bob Baker Marionette Theater• 1923• Richard R.F. Lehman

“A very informative article on the theatre from www.LosAngelesTheatres.blogspot.com
“The theatre opened in 1923 as the York Theatre with John Sugar Amusement Co. as the initial operator. It's on the north side of York Blvd. just west of Avenue 50. The architect is listed as Richard R.F. Lehman. The building has 7,480 s.f. on the main floor and 2,000 s.f. on the booth level.

The interior got a moderne re-do sometime in the 30s that obliterated nearly all of the original decor. It's unknown when it closed as a a full time film house.

The L.A. Times reports that the building was later used as a barber shop as well as an organ building and repair shop. In 1985 it became the Pyong Kang Korean church. The church was out in 2017 and the building was placed on the market in 2018. It sold in November of that same year.

In February 2019 it was announced that the Bob Baker Marionette Theatre signed a 10 year lease on the building.

A estação de Saycan faz parte da linha Tronco Porto Alegre - Uruguaiana, no seu trecho final construído entre as estações de Cacequi e Alegrete.
.
A obra desta monumental estrada de ferro havia começado 30 anos antes, em 1877, desde a margem direita do rio Taquari, onde hoje é General Câmara, sendo realizada por etapas: 1883 até Cachoeira do Sul, 1885 Santa Maria e 1890 Cacequi. Em 1894 o novo governo republicano decide realizar estudos detalhados dos desempenhos das ferrovias sob sua administração, entre elas a EF Porto Alegre Uruguaiana, decidindo paralisar as suas obras em 1897. 
.
Em 1898 a linha foi arrendada à Cie Auxiliaire. Nesta época, o trecho entre Uruguaiana e Alegrete estava praticamente concluído, sendo inclusive operado de forma provisória e irregular. Let's take a look at some of the Central's larger road power.

For the longest time, the Central only rostered one SD60 locomotive. When the opportunity rose to purchase a group of second-hand SD60's, the CERA acquired them. CERA 6001 is one of three former HLCX SD60 units purchased after lease from Norfolk Southern. The unit dates back to September of 1986 when EMD built the locomotive for the Chicago & Northwestern railroad as their 8052 to be used in coal train service. Union Pacific absorbed the CNW in 1996, where the CNW 8052 was patched and renumbered to the UP 5967. After a lease expiration, the unit went to Helm Financial, spending most of its time on eastern roads CSX and NS. In the early 2010's, NS purchased a large group of SD60's from HLCX for use in rebuilding, but three from the CNW bunch were sold to the CERA. This SD60 trio was the stepping stone to the motive power update the CERA has needed to keep trains rolling efficiently.

OFOX 2788 is an SD40M-2 rebuild, constructed by EMD in September of 1968 for the Seaboard Coast Line as SD45 number 2011. From the SCL to the SBD, the 2011 was rebuilt as an SD40-2 locomotive for the Union Pacific as their 2788. After a short carrier on the UP, Capital Equipment Finance aquired it for their lease fleet, wearing both CEFX and CITX (Commercial Investment Trust) markings. The unit spent most of its time with CSX during the early 2000's and into the early 2010's. In 2013 the unit was passed to Residco ownership, using the marks OFOX. Fast forward to the present and OFOX 2788 works for the CERA.

The Central has a decent history with buying used EMD locomotives from Canadian Pacific. One of the earlier acquisitions dates back to 2011 when they picked up the present day CERA 4081. This SD40-2 locomotive was built in October of 1974 for the Soo Line railroad, delivered as the 779. The 779 traded its Soo colors for a fresh coat of CP's "Dual Flag" scheme in 1993. CP still kept it rostered as the 779. The most glaring feature about this unit is its lack of dynamic brakes, which usually keeps the 4081 off the long road trains. The simple red scheme is accented with Central nose and carbody logos, and looks good for its age, with other additional key spotting features giving away its heritage.

Regardless of scale, the basic approach to powered brass model train locomotives rarely changes, the frame and body is part of the current collection path, and heck it can be a pain in the arse. Ever wonder why I bang on about soldering metal models? Artisans with their adhesives get a little shirty (shitty ? ) when I can't quote on their repair.

I'm re-assembling an O Scale Santa Fe 1800 class and before I get too far along, here is one step that all brass locos receive.

In O Scale 25 thou is fine, smaller scales 10 or 15 thou bronze wire is usually ok. I solder a V shaped piece of bronze to the stretcher to bear against the live wheels. Careful adjustment to make sure only enough pressure is available to keep the wire against the wheel without introducing much drag.
